subject.title: fix(signal): derive streamContainerEvents handshakeTimeout from caller timeoutMs

question: Should an explicit Signal stream `timeoutMs` fully control the WebSocket opening-handshake deadline, including values longer than the previous 30-second cap?
rationale: The implementation is correct and well-proven, but accepting caller values above 30 seconds intentionally changes how long existing configured streams can remain stalled before the reconnect loop resumes.

options.title: Honor the caller budget
options.body: Land the patch so explicit shorter and longer timeout values control the stream handshake while omission remains at 30 seconds.

options.title: Keep the 30-second cap
options.body: Reject or revise the patch to clamp longer caller values, preserving current reconnect timing but leaving `timeoutMs` only partially honored.

recommendation.title: Honor the caller budget
recommendation.body: Land the patch so explicit shorter and longer timeout values control the stream handshake while omission remains at 30 seconds.
